p.src: At that moment Shi Jin said, “What are we to do?” Zhu Wu and the other two chiefs knelt and replied, “Brother, you are an innocent man. Do not let us bring trouble upon you. Bind the three of us with ropes and take us out to claim the reward, so that you are spared disgrace on our account.” Shi Jin said, “How could I do that! If I did, it would seem that I had lured you here only to seize you and claim the reward, and I would be mocked by everyone under heaven. If I die, I shall die with you; if I live, I shall live with you. Rise and set your minds at ease. We shall find another way around this. First let me ask how this came about and what lies behind it.”

p.src: Shi Jin climbed the ladder and called down, “You two constables, why have you come to raid my manor in the dead of night?” The two constables answered, “Young Master, are you still denying it? The accuser, Li Ji, is right here.” Shi Jin shouted, “Li Ji, how dare you falsely accuse an innocent man?” Li Ji answered, “I knew nothing of it at first. I found Wang Si’s reply in the woods and happened to examine it before the county offices; that is how the affair came to light.” Shi Jin summoned Wang Si and demanded, “You said there was no reply. How is it that there was a letter after all?” Wang Si said, “Your servant was drunk at the time and forgot about the reply.” Shi Jin roared, “You brute! What are we to do now?” Outside, the constables and their men knew how formidable Shi Jin was and dared not rush into the manor to make arrests. The three chiefs gestured and said, “Answer those men outside for now.” Shi Jin understood. From the ladder he called, “You two constables, make no disturbance. Draw back for the moment. I shall bind myself and come out to be taken before the authorities, and you may claim your reward.” The two constables were afraid of Shi Jin and could only answer, “We have no quarrel with you. We shall wait for you to come out bound, and then go together to claim the reward.” Shi Jin descended the ladder and returned to the main hall. First he had Wang Si taken into the rear garden, where he killed him with a single stroke of his blade. Then he ordered the many retainers to gather at once whatever valuables and belongings the manor contained and pack everything up, while thirty or forty torches were lit. Inside the manor, Shi Jin and the three chiefs armed themselves from head to foot, each girding on a saber from the weapon rack, taking up a long-handled broadsword, and tightening his gear; then they set fire to the thatched buildings behind the manor. Each of the retainers tied up his bundle. When the men outside saw flames rising within, they all ran around to the rear to look. Meanwhile, Shi Jin set fire to the central hall as well, flung open the manor gates, and charged out with a mighty battle cry.

p.src: Shi Jin led the way, Zhu Wu and Yang Chun held the center, and Chen Da brought up the rear. Together with the bandits and manor retainers, they drove and battered through the enemy, striking east and west. Shi Jin was a veritable tiger—who could possibly withstand him? With flames leaping wildly behind them, they hacked open a path and burst through, straight into the two constables and Li Ji. Shi Jin flew into a rage at the sight of them—“When enemies meet, their eyes see all the clearer.” Realizing the tide had turned against them, the two constables wheeled around and fled. Li Ji too was about to turn and run, but Shi Jin was already upon him. His long-handled blade rose and fell, cleaving Li Ji in two. Just as the two constables were about to escape, Chen Da and Yang Chun caught them. Each struck down one man with his long-handled blade, ending both their lives. The county commandant was so terrified that he galloped away. The soldiers dared not advance. Each fled for his life and scattered, no one knew where. Shi Jin led his company onward, fighting as they went. The government troops dared not pursue and scattered in every direction. Shi Jin, Zhu Wu, Chen Da, Yang Chun, and all the manor retainers reached the stronghold on Mount Shaohua and sat down. Only after a while did they recover their breath. Once Zhu Wu and the others were inside the stronghold, they hurriedly ordered their men to slaughter cattle and horses and prepare a feast of celebration. Of that there is no more to tell.

p.src: Several days passed. Shi Jin reflected, “In my haste to save those three men, I set fire to my manor. Though I brought away some valuables and property, all the heavier possessions are gone.” He wavered inwardly, feeling that he could not remain there indefinitely, and said to Zhu Wu and the others, “My master, Arms Instructor Wang, serves in the Military Commissioner’s headquarters in Guanxi. I had meant to seek him earlier, but my father’s death prevented me from going. Now that my property and manor have been utterly destroyed, I mean to go and find him.” Zhu Wu and the other two said, “Brother, do not go. Stay in our stronghold for a while, and then we can discuss what is to be done. If you do not wish to become an outlaw, then once matters have quieted down, we shall rebuild your manor for you, and you can return to life as an honest citizen.” Shi Jin said, “Your kindness is heartfelt, but my resolve to leave cannot be shaken. If I find my master, I hope to secure a position there and enjoy some measure of happiness for the rest of my life.” Zhu Wu said, “Brother, why not become the chief of this stronghold? Would that not be a happy life? I fear only that our stronghold is too small to accommodate a man of your stature.” Shi Jin said, “I am an honorable and unblemished man. How could I consent to defile the body bequeathed to me by my parents? Never again speak of persuading me to become an outlaw.” Shi Jin stayed a few more days, but remained determined to leave. For all their earnest entreaties, Zhu Wu and the others could not detain him. All the manor retainers who had accompanied Shi Jin remained at the mountain stronghold; he merely gathered a little silver, tied it into a bundle, and entrusted all the rest of his wealth to the stronghold.

p.src: Shi Jin wore a broad white Fanyang felt hat sprinkled with a tuft of red tassels; beneath it his hair was wrapped in a deep-blue soft kerchief with raised corners, and a bright-yellow braided cord hung at his neck. He wore a white ramie-silk battle robe with double upper collars and fastened at his waist a five-finger-wide plum-red braided sash. Blue-and-white striped leggings bound his feet, over which he wore multi-eared hemp shoes fit for scaling mountains and crossing rough ground. At his hip hung a goose-feather saber with a broad, cymbal-shaped brass guard. With his bundle on his back and a long-handled broadsword in hand, he bade farewell to Zhu Wu and the other two. The whole band escorted him down the mountain. Zhu Wu and the others parted from him in tears, then returned to their stronghold.

p.src: Rugged mountain ridges, desolate and lonely villages. Wrapped in cloud and mist, he lodged by night in wild woods; beneath the dawn moon, he climbed perilous paths. Hurrying on at sunset, he heard dogs bark; pressed onward through hard frost at dawn, he heard cocks crow.

p.src: On the road, Shi Jin inevitably ate when hungry, drank when thirsty, lodged at night, and traveled at dawn. Traveling alone for more than half a month, he arrived at Weizhou. “There is a Military Commissioner’s headquarters here too. Could my master, Arms Instructor Wang, be here?” Shi Jin entered the city and saw that it had the usual bustling streets and marketplaces. He noticed a small teahouse standing at a crossroads. Shi Jin entered the teahouse, chose a seat, and sat down. The tea server asked, “What tea would you like, sir?” Shi Jin said, “Bring me a cup of steeped tea.” The server prepared the tea and placed it before Shi Jin. Shi Jin asked, “Where is the Military Commissioner’s headquarters?” The server said, “It is just up ahead.” Shi Jin said, “May I ask whether there is an arms instructor named Wang Jin, from the Eastern Capital, serving in the headquarters?” The server replied, “There are a great many arms instructors in that headquarters, including three or four surnamed Wang. I do not know which one is Wang Jin.”

p.src: Around his head he wore a sesame-colored gauze turban patterned with swastikas, with two twisted gold rings of Taiyuan workmanship behind it. Over his body was a parrot-green silk battle robe; around his waist, a dark-blue double-stranded military-and-civilian sash; and on his feet, a pair of tawny four-seamed boots of eagle-claw leather. He had a round face, large ears, a straight nose, a square mouth, and a luxuriant raccoon-dog beard along his cheeks; he stood eight feet tall, with a waist ten spans around.

p.src: The man entered the teahouse and sat down. The tea waiter said, “Sir, if you seek Instructor Wang, just ask this commandant here. He knows everyone.” Shi Jin hurriedly rose and saluted him. “Please sit, sir, and allow me to offer you tea.” Seeing that Shi Jin was tall, powerfully built, and plainly a gallant fellow, the man came over and exchanged salutations with him. The two sat down. Shi Jin said, “Forgive my boldness, sir, but may I ask your honored name?” The man replied, “I am a commandant in the Military Commissioner’s headquarters. My surname is Lu, and my given name is Da. And may I ask, brother, what is your surname?” Shi Jin said, “I am a native of Huayin County in Hua Prefecture. My surname is Shi and my given name is Jin. May I ask, sir: I have a master named Wang Jin, formerly an instructor of the eight hundred thousand Imperial Guards in the Eastern Capital. Is he here in this Military Commissioner’s headquarters or not?” Commandant Lu said, “Brother, can you be none other than Young Master Shi of Shi Family Village, the man called ‘Nine-Tattooed Dragon’?” Shi Jin bowed. “That is I.” Commandant Lu hastily returned the salute and said, “Hearing of a man is not as good as meeting him, and meeting him surpasses all one has heard. This Instructor Wang you seek—would he be Wang Jin, who incurred Grand Marshal Gao’s enmity in the Eastern Capital?” Shi Jin said, “That is the very man.” Lu Da said, “I too have heard his name. But that brother is not here. I hear that he serves under the Senior Military Commissioner in Yan’an Prefecture. Our Weizhou here is garrisoned by the Junior Military Commissioner, so the man is not here. Since you are Young Master Shi, whose fine reputation I have so often heard, come out with me and drink a cup of wine.” Commandant Lu took Shi Jin by the hand and led him out of the teahouse. Lu Da looked back and said, “I will settle the tea money with you later.” The tea waiter answered, “Drink whenever you please, Commandant. Go on; there is no need to worry.”

p.src: The two linked arms and left the teahouse. After walking thirty or fifty paces along the street, they saw a crowd gathered around an open space. Shi Jin said, “Elder brother, let us take a look.” They parted the crowd and looked inside. In the middle stood a man with some ten cudgels propped around him; a dozen or more medicinal plasters were spread on the ground in a tray, with a paper sign stuck above them. He was one of those wandering martial performers who sold medicines while displaying their skill with spear and staff. At a glance Shi Jin recognized him: it was the master who had first initiated him into martial arts, Li Zhong, called “Tiger-Slaying General.” From within the crowd Shi Jin called, “Master! It has been a long time.” Li Zhong said, “Worthy brother, how did you come here?” Commandant Lu said, “Since you are Young Master Shi’s teacher, come drink three cups with us.” Li Zhong said, “Let me sell these plasters and collect some money; then I shall go with you, Commandant.” Lu Da said, “Who has the patience to wait for you? If you are coming, come now.” Li Zhong said, “This is how I earn my bread; I have no other choice. Go on ahead, Commandant, and I will find you presently. Worthy brother, you go ahead with the Commandant.” Lu Da lost his temper, shoved one of the onlookers sprawling, and cursed, “You bastards, unclench your arses and clear out! Anyone who stays gets a beating from me!” When the crowd saw it was Commandant Lu, they scattered in a rush. Seeing Lu Da’s ferocity, Li Zhong dared to be angry but not to speak. He could only force a smile and say, “What an impatient man!” He thereupon packed up his gear and medicine bag and left his spears and staffs in safekeeping. p.src: The three went upstairs in the Pan family tavern, chose a neat private room, and sat down. Commandant Lu took the place of honor, Li Zhong sat opposite him, and Shi Jin sat below them. The waiter bowed a greeting. Recognizing Commandant Lu, he asked, “Commandant, how much wine shall I draw?” Lu Da said, “Bring four measures to begin with, and set out vegetables, fruit, and dishes to go with the wine.” The waiter asked again, “Sir, what would you like for the main dishes?” Lu Da said, “Why ask? Whatever you have, just bring it. We will reckon up the whole bill and pay you afterward. This fellow does nothing but chatter.” The waiter went downstairs and soon brought up warmed wine; every savory meat dish fit to eat was brought without stint until the whole table was covered. After the three had drunk several cups, they chatted idly and compared techniques of the spear. Just as their talk grew lively, they heard someone sobbing and weeping in the adjoining room. Lu Da became irritated and flung the saucers and wine cups onto the floorboards. Hearing the noise, the waiter hurried upstairs and found Commandant Lu seething with anger. Folding his hands respectfully, the waiter asked, “What do you require, sir? Give the order and I will procure it.” Lu Da said, “What do I require? You ought to know who I am. Why have you let someone whine and cry next door, spoiling our drinking? Surely I have never shorted you on the wine money!” The waiter said, “Please calm your anger, sir. How would I dare let anyone weep and disturb your drinking? Those weeping are a father and daughter who sing from table to table for wine customers. They did not know that you gentlemen were drinking here and, overcome for a moment by their troubles, began to cry.” Commandant Lu said, “What a strange business! Call them here to me.”

p.src: Her cloudlike hair was loosely dressed, with a green-jade hairpin thrust through it; her slender waist swayed gracefully, girdled by a six-panel skirt of red gauze. An old plain-white jacket enfolded her snowy body, and pale-yellow soft stockings set off her tiny embroidered shoes. Her mothlike brows were tightly knit, and pearls fell from her brimming, tearful eyes; her powdered face hung low, while her delicate fragrant flesh wasted away like melting jade and snow. If she was not stricken by the sorrows of rain and cloud, then surely long-gathered care and resentment burdened her heart.

p.src: The woman wiped away her tears, stepped forward, and made three deep bows. The old man also came forward and paid his respects. Lu Da asked, “Where are you two from? Why are you weeping?” The woman replied, “You do not know our plight, sir. Allow me to tell you: I am a native of the Eastern Capital. I came with my parents to Weizhou to seek refuge with relatives, only to find that they had moved away to the Southern Capital. My mother fell ill and died at an inn, leaving my father and me stranded here to suffer. There is a wealthy man here, Master Zheng, known as ‘The Suppressor of the West.’ When he saw me, he sent men to force a match upon us and demanded that I become his concubine. But though he drew up a bond for three thousand strings of cash, the money was fictitious while the contract was real, and so he took possession of me. Before three months had passed, his wife, a most vicious woman, had me beaten and driven out. She would not let us remain together and ordered the innkeeper to collect from us the original three thousand strings supposedly paid for my person. My father is timid and cannot contend with him, while he has both wealth and power. We never received a single coin from him in the first place; where could we find the money to repay him now? With no other recourse, I have used the few songs my father taught me as a child to go from table to table singing in this winehouse. Whatever money we earn each day, we give most of it to him and retain only a little for my father’s and my expenses. For the past two days there have been few customers, and we have missed his payment deadline. We fear the humiliation we will suffer when he comes to demand his money. My father and I thought of all this misery and had nowhere to voice our grievance, and that is why we wept. We never meant to disturb you, sir. We beg you to forgive us and show us mercy.”

I wondered which great Master Zheng it might be, but it turns out to be Zheng the pig butcher! That filthy scoundrel secured a place under our Junior Commandant and set himself up as a butcher, yet he dares bully people like this!” Turning to Li Zhong and Shi Jin, he said, “You two wait here while I go beat that cur to death. I will be back presently.” Shi Jin and Li Zhong seized him and urged, “Brother, calm your anger. We will deal with him tomorrow.” Only after repeated entreaties did the two manage to restrain him.

p.src: Lu Da then said, “Come here, old man. I will give you some traveling money. How would it be if you returned to the Eastern Capital tomorrow?” The father and daughter pleaded, “If we could return home, you would be like parents who gave us life anew, like father and mother reborn to us. But how could the innkeeper be willing to release us? Master Zheng has made him responsible for collecting the money.” Commandant Lu said, “That is no concern. I have my own way of dealing with it.” He felt about his person, took out five taels of silver, and set them on the table. Looking at Shi Jin, he said, “I did not bring much with me today. If you have silver, lend me some, and I will repay you tomorrow.” Shi Jin said, “What does it matter? There is no need for you to repay me, brother.” He took a ten-tael ingot of silver from his bundle and placed it on the table. Lu Da looked at Li Zhong and said, “You lend me some as well.” Li Zhong felt about his person and brought out two taels of silver. Commandant Lu saw how little it was and said, “You are a grudging sort of fellow.” Lu Da gave Old Jin only the fifteen taels and instructed him, “Take this as traveling money for you and your daughter, and begin packing your belongings. I will come early tomorrow morning to see you both on your way. Let us see what innkeeper dares detain you!” Old Jin and his daughter bowed their thanks and departed.

p.src: Lu Da tossed the two taels of silver back to Li Zhong. The three drank two more measures of wine, then went downstairs and called, “Innkeeper, I will bring the wine money tomorrow and repay you in full.” The proprietor answered repeatedly, “Go as you please, Commandant. Drink without concern. My only fear is that you will not come here to drink on credit.” The three left the Pan Family Winehouse and parted in the street. Shi Jin and Li Zhong each returned to his inn. As for Commandant Lu, he returned to his lodging before the commandant’s residence, went to his room, and lay down in a fury without even eating supper. The landlord did not dare question him.

p.src: Meanwhile, after Old Jin received the fifteen taels of silver, he returned to the inn and settled his daughter in their room. First he went far outside the city and hired a cart. Then he returned, packed their belongings, paid the lodging charge, settled the accounts for firewood and rice, and waited only for dawn the next day. Nothing happened that night. Early the next morning, at the fifth watch, father and daughter rose, lit the fire, prepared their meal, ate, and made themselves ready. As the sky was just beginning to brighten, Commandant Lu came striding into the inn and called loudly, “Waiter! Where is Old Jin lodging?” The waiter called, “Master Jin, the Commandant is here looking for you.” Old Jin opened the door and said, “Commandant, sir, please come inside and sit down.” Lu Da said, “What is there to sit for? If you are going, then go. What are you waiting for?” Old Jin brought out his daughter, shouldered their load, thanked the Commandant, and was about to leave when the waiter blocked their way and said, “Master Jin, where are you going?” Lu Da asked, “Does he owe you money for the room?” The waiter said, “The money owed to me for the room was all settled last night. But he still owes Master Zheng the money for the pledge of his daughter’s person, and I have been made responsible for keeping watch over him!” Commandant Lu said, “I will repay Zheng the Butcher’s money myself. Let this old man return to his native place.” But the waiter refused to let them go. Lu Da flew into a rage, spread his five fingers, and struck the waiter across the face with a single slap, making blood gush from his mouth; then with another punch, he knocked out the two front teeth at the center of his mouth. The waiter scrambled to his feet and fled like a puff of smoke into the inn to hide. The innkeeper did not dare come out to stop him. Old Jin and his daughter hurriedly left the inn, went out of the city, and set off to find the cart they had hired the day before. Lu Da, meanwhile, thought to himself that the waiter might chase after them and bar their way, so he dragged a bench from inside the inn and sat there for four hours. When he reckoned that Master Jin had gone far enough, he finally rose and went straight to Number-One-Scholar Bridge.

p.src: Now Zheng the Butcher kept a shop with two open fronts and two butcher’s blocks, from which hung several slabs of pork. Zheng sat behind the counter by the entrance, watching his dozen or so knife-hands sell meat. Lu Da came up and called, “Zheng the Butcher!” Zheng looked up and, seeing that it was Warden Lu, hurried out from behind the counter, bowed, and said, “Forgive me, Warden.” He ordered an assistant to bring a stool. “Please sit down, Warden.” Lu Da sat down and said, “By His Excellency the Military Commissioner’s command, I require ten catties of lean meat, finely minced, without the least speck of fat in it.” “Certainly,” said Zheng. “You men, quickly choose the best and cut ten catties.” Warden Lu said, “I will not have those filthy fellows lay hands on it. Cut it yourself.” Zheng said, “You are quite right. I shall cut it myself.” He went to the butcher’s block, selected ten catties of lean meat, and painstakingly minced it fine. The tavern boy, his head wrapped in a kerchief, was just coming to Zheng’s house to report what had happened with Old Jin. But when he saw Warden Lu sitting beside the butcher’s block, he dared not approach and could only stand at a distance under the eaves and watch. Zheng spent a full hour cutting it himself, then wrapped it in lotus leaves and said, “Warden, I shall have someone deliver it.” Lu Da said, “Deliver what? Wait! I want another ten catties, all fat this time, without the least scrap of lean in it, and that too must be minced fine.” Zheng said, “I thought the lean meat was perhaps for making wontons at the residence. What use can you have for minced fat?” Lu Da glared at him. “His Excellency gave me his command. Who dares question him?” Zheng said, “Then it must be needed. I shall cut it.” He selected another ten catties of solid fat, minced it just as finely, and wrapped it in lotus leaves. He had labored the whole morning, and by then it was past mealtime. The tavern boy dared not come near, and even the customers who wished to buy meat were afraid to approach. Zheng said, “Have someone carry these for the Warden and deliver them to the residence.” Lu Da said, “I want another ten catties of the choicest soft cartilage. Chop that fine as well, without leaving the least bit of meat on it.” Zheng laughed. “Have you not come here expressly to make sport of me?” At this Lu Da sprang to his feet, seized the two parcels of mince, glared at Zheng, and said, “I came expressly to make sport of you!” He flung both parcels straight into Zheng’s face, and meat rained down in a shower. Zheng flew into a rage; two surges of fury rushed from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head. Unable to contain the raging flames of his senseless wrath, he snatched a sharp boning knife from the block and leaped down with a thud. Warden Lu had already strode out into the street. Not one of the neighbors or the dozen shopmen dared step forward to intervene. Passersby on both sides stopped in their tracks, while the tavern boy too stood frozen with fright.

p.src: Knife in his right hand, Zheng reached with his left to seize Lu Da. Warden Lu caught that wrist as it came, drove him backward, and kicked him squarely in the lower belly, sending him sprawling into the street. Lu Da stepped forward, planted a foot on his chest, raised a fist as large as a vinegar jar, and looked down at Zheng. “When I first entered the service of the elder Military Commissioner, I rose to become an inspector of the five circuits west of the passes; I had some right to be called ‘Lord of the West.’ But you are merely a knife-wielding butcher who sells meat, a dog of a man, and you too call yourself ‘Lord of the West’! How dared you bully and deceive Jin Cuilian?” With a thud he struck Zheng squarely on the nose. Blood spurted forth and the nose twisted to one side; it was as though an oil-and-sauce shop had opened, with salty, sour, and pungent flavors all pouring out together. Zheng could not struggle free. His sharp knife had fallen aside, and all he could say was, “Well struck!” Lu Da cursed him: “You whoreson! You still dare answer back?” He raised his fist and struck once at the rim of the eye and tip of the brow. The eyelid split and the dark eyeball bulged out; it was as though a silk shop had opened, with red, black, and crimson fabrics all bursting forth. The onlookers on either side feared Warden Lu, and none dared come forward to stop him. Unable to endure any more, Zheng begged for mercy. Lu Da thundered, “Bah! You ruined rogue—had you stood firm against me to the end, I might have spared you; but since you beg me for mercy, I shall show you none!” He struck once more, squarely on the temple. It was as though a grand Buddhist and Daoist service were being held, with stone chimes, cymbals, and gongs all sounding together. When Lu Da looked, Zheng lay rigid on the ground, breathing out but no longer drawing breath, unable to move. Warden Lu pretended otherwise. “You rascal, you are feigning death. I shall hit you again.” But he saw the man’s complexion gradually changing. Lu Da thought, “I meant only to give this fellow a sound beating. I never imagined that three blows would truly kill him. I shall have a lawsuit on my hands, and no one to bring me food in prison. Better slip away while I can.” He turned to leave, then pointed back at Zheng’s corpse and said, “You are feigning death! I shall settle matters with you at leisure.” Still cursing, he strode away. Not one of the neighbors or Zheng’s shopmen dared step forward to stop him. Warden Lu returned to his lodgings and hurriedly bundled up some clothes, traveling money, valuables, and silver. All old clothes and cumbersome articles he left behind. Taking a short staff as tall as his eyebrows, he hurried out through the south gate and vanished like a trail of smoke.

p.src: Meanwhile, the people of Zheng’s household tried for half a day to revive him, but to no avail. He was dead. His family and the neighbors went directly to the prefectural court to lodge a complaint. The prefect had just taken his seat in court. He received the petition, read it, and said, “Lu Da is a warden attached to the Military Commissioner’s residence. I dare not take it upon myself to arrest the killer directly.” The prefect immediately mounted his sedan chair and went to the Military Commissioner’s residence, where he alighted at the gate. The soldiers guarding the gate went inside to announce him. On hearing this, the Military Commissioner ordered that he be shown into the hall, where they exchanged formal greetings. The Military Commissioner asked, “What brings you here?” The prefect reported, “Your Excellency should know that Lu Da, a warden in your residence, struck and killed Zheng the Butcher in the marketplace without cause. Since I had not first reported the matter to Your Excellency, I dared not take it upon myself to arrest the killer.” The Military Commissioner was startled by the news and thought, “Lu Da may be a fine fighter, but his nature is coarse and reckless. Now that he has taken a life, how can I shield him from blame? He must be examined according to law.” The Military Commissioner replied to the prefect, “Lu Da was originally an officer under my father, the elder Military Commissioner. Because I lacked anyone here to assist and protect me, my father transferred him here to serve as a warden. Since he has committed the crime of taking a life, you may arrest and examine him according to the law. If his confession establishes the facts and his sentence has been proposed, my father must also be informed before final judgment is passed. Otherwise, should my father later require this man on the frontier, the affair would reflect badly on us.” The prefect replied, “Once this humble official has investigated the circumstances, I shall duly report them to the elder Military Commissioner before daring to pronounce sentence.”

The case papers were compiled, while officers were dispatched under threat of flogging and a deadline to hunt down the murderer. The complainants were released into the custody of guarantors and sent home. The neighbors were sentenced to flogging for failing to render aid. The landlord and the neighbors of Lu’s lodging were found guilty only of failing to report him. Since Lu Da was at large, urgent general warrants were circulated by express courier, ordering his pursuit on every route. A reward of one thousand strings of cash was offered, and notices recording Lu Da’s age, native place, residence, and appearance were posted everywhere for his arrest. All the others concerned were provisionally released to await further summons. Zheng the Butcher’s relatives went about their mourning rites, of which no more need be said.

p.src: Commandant Lu hurried through several prefectures and provinces; truly, “One fleeing for his life does not choose his road, but makes a home wherever he may.” As the old saying lists the several kinds of desperation: “The hungry do not choose their food, the cold do not choose their clothes, the frightened do not choose their road, and the poor do not choose their wife.” Lu Da, his heart in turmoil, rushed blindly along, with no notion where he might find refuge. After wandering aimlessly for more than half a month, he came on his journey to Yanmen County in Daizhou. p.src: Shoulder against shoulder and back against back, necks craned and heads pressed together. In the teeming throng, wise and foolish could not be told apart; amid the commotion, noble and base were indistinguishable. Stout, foolish Zhang the Third, unable to read, could only shake his head; Short, stunted Li the Fourth stood on tiptoe when he saw the others do so. White-haired old men propped their bearded chins upon their staffs; Young scholars with dark locks took out their writing implements and copied down the listed particulars. p.src: Seeing the crowd packed around the notice at the crossroads, Lu Da squeezed among them to listen. Since he could not read, he heard the others reading aloud: “Yanmen County of Daizhou, acting under orders from the Military Command Office of Taiyuan Prefecture and in receipt of a document from Weizhou, hereby seeks the arrest of Lu Da, the criminal who beat Zheng the Butcher to death, formerly a commandant in the Military Commissioner’s headquarters. Anyone who shelters him at home or provides him lodging and food shall be held guilty of the same crime as the fugitive. Anyone who captures and delivers him, or reports him to the authorities, shall be paid a reward of one thousand strings of cash. …” Commandant Lu had just heard this much when suddenly someone behind him shouted, “Brother Zhang! What are you doing here?” The man clasped him around the waist and dragged him away from the crossroads. Had this man not seen him and hauled him away by force, events would never have led Commandant Lu to shave his head, remove his beard, exchange his murderous name for another, and vex Buddhas and arhats beyond endurance. His Chan staff would smash open every perilous road, and his戒刀 would slay all who dealt injustice. But who was the man who seized Commandant Lu? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
